title: What reached us as children
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What did you read, as a child, that changed how you saw the world?

groups.heading: A child who asks for proof

lines.text: I said that in this chapter the person in the book is transitioning from a child to reaching out for outside sources of information. The trigger, the way it is written, is that the mother takes them to church, and he asks: what do you mean the water was parted? That's not possible.
This child, I said, early on is showing that if it's not science, then it's not valid for him. He begins to figure out the meaning of life and the universe, and he gets into reading philosophers.
I laughed a little about the philosophers he chose: three of probably the most pessimistic on the planet.

I'm always trying to download it into why it is relevant to us in our lives, I said. These three philosophers made a very big impact on his life. If I ask you: what are the three most impactful books you have read in your life? Be thinking about that.

A student said it was giving a good background: I'm already seeing a little better how he thinks. I said: it is only relevant because it is what he has read. They are the filters for how he makes decisions, and you can see how he constructed his mind from an early age.
What are your three books, and what do they say about you?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the three books or conversations that changed you most.
Write how they filter your decisions today.
Write one book you will give someone you lead.

check.q: What did the child in the book ask about?
choices: How the water could have parted

check.q: What did I say about the philosophers the person chose?
What did I say the books are for how he makes decisions?

recap: Know the books and moments that filter your decisions.
